_note: Serve-path fetchers that return a usable-looking value when the database is
unreachable, so a caller cannot tell 'we looked and found nothing' from 'we
could not look'. SHRINK-ONLY: repair a fetcher and REMOVE it from this list.
Adding a name is not the fix and tests/test_serve_path_fails_closed.py will
fail a newly added one on day one.
Measured 2026-08-15 against a connection whose cursor() raises. The two that
already refuse correctly are fetch_dcp_setbacks and fetch_tax_thresholds,
WHY IT MATTERS AT THE CALLER: services/conveyancing.py wraps each fetch in
try/except and sets _failed[name] = False on the success path. A fetcher
that swallows its own exception returns NORMALLY, so the except never fires
and the system records a SUCCESSFUL check that found nothing.
fetch_heritage_postgis is the sharp one - it returns has_heritage: False,
which renders as 'not heritage listed' when the truth is 'we could not ask'.
